---
layout: null
permalink: /llms.txt
sitemap: false
---
{%- comment -%}
  This site owns its own llms.txt rather than using the one
  jekyll-agent-markdown generates, because the index also lists posts from
  notes.ghinda.com and allaboutcoding.ghinda.com. The gem can't know about
  those: it never touches the network, so external items are fetched by
  bin/fetch_feeds into _data/external_posts.yml (CI refreshes it every 3h).

  agent_markdown.llms_txt is set to false in _config.yml so the gem doesn't
  fight this file for /llms.txt. The gem still exports the per-post .md
  siblings, and it hands us their URLs via post.agent_markdown_url — which is
  nil for opted-out or colliding posts, so the `if` below keeps this index
  honest without duplicating the gem's rules.

  Titles get their square brackets escaped so a future title can't end the
  Markdown link text early; URLs get parentheses percent-encoded for the same
  reason. Neither appears in the current data — this is insurance.

  External URLs are normalized before ".md" is appended: query and fragment are
  dropped, then `split: "/" | join: "/"` removes any trailing slash, because
  Ruby's String#split discards trailing empty fields. allaboutcoding.ghinda.com
  serves its URLs with a trailing slash and notes.ghinda.com without, so both
  shapes have to land on the same ".md". Do NOT reach for `remove_last` here:
  Jekyll 4.4 pins Liquid 4.0.4, which does not have that filter, and Liquid
  passes a value through unknown filters silently — it produced "/slug/.md" on
  every allaboutcoding link with a green build.
{%- endcomment -%}
# {{ site.title }}

> {{ site.description | normalize_whitespace | strip }}

## Articles

> Posts published on this site. Each link points at the post's Markdown source.

{% for post in site.posts -%}
{%- if post.agent_markdown_url -%}
{%- assign title = post.title | normalize_whitespace | replace: "[", "\[" | replace: "]", "\]" -%}
{%- assign url = post.agent_markdown_url | absolute_url | replace: "(", "%28" | replace: ")", "%29" -%}
- [{{ title }}]({{ url }}) | Published at: {{ post.date | date: "%Y-%m-%d" }}
{% endif -%}
{%- endfor %}
## Writing elsewhere

> Recent posts from my other sites, also linked to their Markdown source.

{% assign externals = site.data.external_posts | sort: "date" | reverse -%}
{%- for item in externals -%}
{%- if item.url and item.title and item.date -%}
{%- assign title = item.title | normalize_whitespace | replace: "[", "\[" | replace: "]", "\]" -%}
{%- assign base = item.url | split: "?" | first | split: "#" | first | split: "/" | join: "/" -%}
{%- assign url = base | append: ".md" | replace: "(", "%28" | replace: ")", "%29" -%}
- [{{ title }}]({{ url }}) | Published at: {{ item.date | date: "%Y-%m-%d" }}
{% endif -%}
{%- endfor -%}
